claim.value: If missing attachments recur when ambiguity is restored in simulation and improve when clarity is restored again, that sequence would provide an additional signal specific to the simulation.
claim.scope: A conditional simulated reversal-and-restoration outcome, without asserting that it occurred or generalizes quantitatively to live work.

provenance.rationale: P015 states the conditional simulation-specific signal; P014 identifies the attachment outcome; P029 supplies the limit on quantitative generalization to live work.

signal_basis.value: Alternate unclear and clear attachment responsibility across comparable fictitious tasks in a safe simulation, observing recurrence of missing attachments under restored ambiguity and improvement when clarity returns.
signal_basis.scope: Simulation only, without weakening live controls; stop if real purchases could be affected. The sequence does not establish live effect magnitude or exclude alternative causes.

provenance.rationale: The cited spans supply the simulated manipulation, comparable tasks, observed sequence, safety boundaries and inferential limits.
The claim is supported under the assumed signal; no separate unresolved empirical relation is needed.

rationale: Assuming the specified operation and outcome, recurrence and improvement accompanying reversal and restoration provide an additional signal within the simulation. The claim asserts neither conclusive causation nor a quantitative live-work effect, so the mapping's acknowledged alternatives do not defeat this limited warrant.
uncertainty: Alternative causes and transfer to live work remain unresolved, but neither must be settled to identify the sequence as a simulation-specific signal.
